To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) window opening behaviour in naturally ventilated offices is strongly related to outdoor temperature; (2) occupants' window opening is more frequent in the morning, in the afternoon, in the summer and when the office is occupied; (3) occupants' window behaviour can be predicted by a simple stochastic model; (4) window opening behaviour is also influenced by the window orientation.
Occupants of the building opened the windows more in summer than in winter, more in the afternoon and evening than in the morning, and more on working days than on weekend days.
Occupants' behaviour is strongly influenced by the outdoor air temperature and the time of a day.
